strengths: Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation across 7 datasets and 4 MIM frameworks with careful experimental design and extensive ablations
Excellent systematic analysis that unifies multiple existing methods under a common framework, providing valuable insights into their relationships
Clear identification of LP's limitation in spatial feature aggregation and well-motivated use of attention mechanisms as a solution
Strong empirical results demonstrating significant accuracy-efficiency trade-offs (10-13.6% improvement on ImageNet-1k with fewer parameters)
Insightful correlation analysis between attention map quality (localization/entropy) and classification performance provides theoretical grounding
Excellent visualizations and interpretability with clear attention maps demonstrating diverse spatial focus across methods
Strong reproducibility with detailed implementation details and thorough supplementary material
weaknesses: Limited novelty: EP applies standard MHCA with learnable queries rather than proposing fundamentally new mechanisms; similar ideas already present in AIM, CAE, CLIP
Modest improvements over competing attention-based methods, particularly CAE and CLIP, though substantial gains versus LP
Incomplete theoretical justification for why spatial localization matters for MIM representations beyond empirical correlation
Underexplored design space: query initialization sensitivity, dimension choices, and rationale for specific formulation (Eq. 7-8) lack investigation
Computational cost analysis incomplete: FLOPs reported but actual wall-clock time and memory consumption details missing; 10x reduction claim needs rigorous justification
Narrow scope limited to image classification; no analysis of transfer to other downstream tasks or whether attention patterns generalize
Lacks statistical analysis: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests; important given sometimes-marginal improvements
Overclaimed interpretability: some attention maps remain noisy and only partially interpretable despite claims of interpretability
Dense mathematical notation in Section 3 that could benefit from clearer intuitive explanations; key results relegated to appendix

strengths: Comprehensive empirical benchmark of attentive probing methods across diverse pre-training paradigms and datasets, providing valuable systematization of the method design space
Well-motivated problem clearly articulating the efficiency vs. accuracy trade-off in representation evaluation
Practical method (EP) that is elegantly simple yet achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with reduced parameters, showing consistent improvements across multiple datasets
Novel analysis of attention complementarity and interpretability, with compelling visualizations showing how different queries specialize in distinct object regions
Extensive experimental analysis including Pareto frontiers, layer-wise probing, low-shot scenarios, and attention quality metrics that provide useful insights
Good generalization demonstrated across 7+ datasets, multiple pre-training methods (supervised, self-supervised, vision-language), and different model architectures
Clear presentation and strong reproducibility with implementation details and standard evaluation protocols
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: EP is a straightforward simplification of MHCA by removing key transformation matrices, representing an incremental contribution rather than a fundamental methodological advance

Severe scope limitation to frozen pre-trained backbones only—no fine-tuning experiments to validate whether probing insights transfer to practical downstream performance, limiting real-world applicability

Single-domain evaluation restricted to image classification with no evaluation on detection, segmentation, or other vision tasks, and no multimodal applications despite mentioning vision-language models
Insufficient analysis of why EP works mechanistically—while complementarity is shown, the causal link between diverse attention maps and improved accuracy is not established
Missing critical comparisons with parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods (LoRA, prefix-tuning, adapters) that are more practically relevant than frozen-backbone probing
Weak statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, error bars, or significance testing; unclear if multiple random seeds used; small differences between methods lack statistical validation
Incomplete practical analysis: FLOPs reported but no actual wall-clock time, memory usage comparisons, or evidence that parameter reduction translates to real speedups in practice
Weak connection to practical relevance: no demonstration that efficient probing correlates with fine-tuning performance or that efficiency gains matter in downstream applications
Presentation issues: Table 1 is dense and hard to parse; notation inconsistencies; relationship between EP variants (EP₁₆, EP₃₂, etc.) not clearly motivated; some figures difficult to read
Limited analysis of failure modes, sensitivity to hyperparameters, and when EP might not be suitable—Figure 13 hints at this but lacks depth

strengths: Comprehensive empirical benchmark comparing diverse attentive probing methods - first systematic study of this scope providing valuable reference for the community
Simple yet effective method (EP) with clear motivation: eliminates redundant projections while maintaining/improving accuracy with fewer parameters
Strong and consistent experimental results across 7 datasets with 24.3% accuracy improvement over linear probing baseline
Thorough empirical analysis including attention quality correlation, complementarity metrics, entropy analysis, and layer-wise probing that provides good intuition about model behavior
Rigorous experimental protocol with extensive ablations, hyperparameter search across ranges (0.1-5.0), and fair comparison against diverse baselines
Excellent reproducibility with detailed implementation details, learning schedules, and clear evaluation protocols enabling reproduction
Well-organized presentation with clear figures, systematic tables, and extensive appendix material covering additional methods and analysis
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: EP is fundamentally a straightforward modification (learnable queries replacing projection matrices) within existing MHCA framework - incremental contribution despite effectiveness
Narrow experimental scope limited to image classification only - no exploration of generalization to NLP, multimodal learning, or other domains raises generalizability concerns
Lacks theoretical justification for why transformation-free design works better - explanation remains primarily empirical without formal analysis
Evaluation restricted to frozen backbone setting; practical fine-tuning scenarios and realistic deployment considerations are underexplored
Missing comparative analysis with broader parameter-efficient methods (LoRA variants, prompt-based approaches) and insufficient ablation isolating individual design choice contributions
Modest improvements on smaller datasets (CUB200, Cars196) and absence of statistical significance testing weakens generalization claims
Limited investigation into complementarity mechanism and why it specifically emerges in EP; insufficient analysis of failure modes and scenarios where existing methods might be preferable

strengths: First comprehensive benchmark of attentive probing methods across multiple pre-training paradigms, evaluation protocols, and datasets—providing valuable insights for practitioners
Extensive and rigorous experimental validation with fair comparisons across ImageNet-1K and seven additional datasets, using consistent evaluation methodology
Efficient Probing is practical and empirically effective, achieving strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs (e.g., 75.6% on ImageNet-1K with 750K parameters, 4× fewer than linear probing)
Thorough empirical analysis including accuracy-parameter trade-offs, localization quality, complementarity metrics, entropy analysis, and layer-wise probing that provide useful insights
Interpretable attention maps showing that different queries specialize in distinct object regions, with visualizations effectively demonstrating learned structure
Fast convergence: EP reaches near-optimal performance in 10 epochs versus 90 for standard linear probing, offering practical computational benefits
Well-organized presentation with clear motivation, informative figures, and comprehensive appendices providing additional experimental details and analysis
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: multi-query cross-attention for feature aggregation is not particularly novel; the core contribution is essentially a learnable attention pooling mechanism without strong conceptual innovation

Insufficient justification for design choices: unclear why cross-attention is superior to alternatives (learned pooling, gating, slot attention); missing connections to related attention-based pooling literature

Narrow experimental scope: restricted to frozen backbone evaluation on image classification; no dense prediction tasks (segmentation, detection), multimodal settings, or fine-tuning scenarios where strategies might differ

Lacks deep mechanistic understanding: shows that queries specialize in different regions but not why this emergent behavior occurs; insufficient investigation into failure modes or when EP underperforms
Questionable complementarity analysis: L2 distance metric is somewhat arbitrary; unclear why this metric is appropriate or whether complementarity directly drives performance gains

Missing systematic ablations: insufficient analysis of why EP fundamentally outperforms simpler alternatives in Table B; sensitivity to design choices (number of queries M, dimensionality D_e) is incomplete
No statistical significance testing: results lack error bars, confidence intervals, or variance estimates, making it difficult to assess stability and significance of improvements

Scattered scope and presentation: paper covers many topics (multiple pooling variants, complementarity, entropy, Matryoshka learning) causing it to feel unfocused; important design analyses relegated to appendices
